newsitem.title: USA: Two Merrill Lynch officials not SEC targets - source.
newsitem.headline: Two Merrill Lynch officials not SEC targets - source.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission has decided not to pursue charges against two senior Merrill Lynch & Co executives in connection with the agency's long-running Orange County, Calif., bankruptcy investigation, sources said Sunday.

The executives -- Richard Fuscone, a managing director who headed the firm's global debt markets and derivatives unit, and Robert Simonson, a managing director and the former top money markets trader -- are no longer targets in the SEC probe, sources familiar with the investigation said.
Both Merrill Lynch executives had received so-called Wells notices. A Wells notice informs its recipient that SEC staff intends to recommend enforcement action to commissioners.
In addition to the two executives, Merrill Lynch -- the firm -- received a Wells notice. Sources said the SEC would press ahead with its investigation of the brokerage giant.
Orange County shocked Wall Street in December 1994 when it filed for bankruptcy after losing more than $1.6 billion on risky investments made by its then-treasurer, Robert Citron.
The county emerged from bankruptcy one year ago.
Last week Merrill Lynch agreed to pay $30 million to settle a 2-1/2-year investigation by the Orange County district attorney into the county's bankruptcy debacle.
The separate SEC investigation has focused on Orange County bond deals underwritten by Merrill Lynch, and on alleged disclosure violations in the offering documents.
Merrill Lynch maintains that the offerings were done properly.
Several firms besides Merrill Lynch have also received Wells notices, including CS First Boston Corp.
